prompt:
A German woman in her fifties stands on the grey stone pavement of a Berlin
street corner, seen from the waist up, three quarters turned to her left,
right of centre in a vertical frame. A dark navy wool coat over a white top,
a cream tote bag hanging from her forearm, her hair tied back. Her face is
indignant and polite at once, and she looks at a point beyond the left edge
of the frame, away from the camera.

The pavement fills the whole foreground: worn pale grey stone slabs with a
border of small square cobbles, running from edge to edge of the picture up
to the hem of her coat. A straight granite kerb, a plain pale stone lip,
crosses the picture horizontally just behind her coat. Past that kerb, higher
in the frame and further from the camera, a red asphalt lane runs across and
away to the right, and past it the grey asphalt of the road.

Beside her, a pedestrian traffic light stands on a bare grey pole, its black
housing holding two round lenses, the upper one lit and glowing an even plain
red. Behind her the pavement runs on with parked bicycles along a plain pale
building front. Daylight, overcast and flat.
